stem: Meena has a sore throat and fever. Her mother wants to give her leftover antibiotic tablets from an earlier illness. The doctor advises against this. Why should antibiotics be taken only when a doctor prescribes them for a bacterial infection?

options.text: Antibiotics work against every infection, so taking them early always cures the illness faster.
Antibiotics kill bacteria, and careless use can let resistant bacteria develop, making future infections harder to treat.
Antibiotics first act on the throat and then on the stomach, so they must be taken with food.
Antibiotics become stronger each time they are used, so frequent use keeps them powerful.

teacher.key_rationale: B states the correct decision rule: antibiotics target bacteria and indiscriminate use breeds resistance, reducing effectiveness. A is the trap for students who swap the sibling claim that antibiotics suit every infection; C and D misdescribe how antibiotics act.
